title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck is studying the conjectural motivic Galois group G of motives over F_p. It sits in 0 -> G° -> G -> Ẑ -> 0. G is of multiplicative type, dual to the group Γ of Weil numbers (in Q̄*). There are maps G_m --i--> G --ε--> G_m with εi(λ)=λ², dual to Z --ε*--> Γ --i*--> Z, where ε*(1)=p and |λ| = p^{i*(λ)/2} (i* is the weight). Γ° = Ker i* is the group of weight-0 Weil numbers, which he calls 'p-unités de Weil'. The kernel group H, with identity part H° = H/μ2, is dual to Γ°/(roots of unity) = M.

This page computes H²(Q,H) for such a group of multiplicative type. The likely purpose is to locate the cohomology class that obstructs a Q-valued fibre functor on the category of motives over F_p, i.e. the class of the motivic Galois gerbe.

1. He writes H²(Q,H) = lim_K H²(Gal(K/Q), K*⊗M̌), where M̌ is the cocharacter module, so K*⊗M̌ = H(K) at finite level.

2. He applies the idèle/idèle-class sequence 0 -> K* -> I -> C -> 0 tensored with M̌, and takes the long exact sequence in G-cohomology.

3. Tate–Nakayama gives H^r(G, C⊗M̌) ≅ Ĥ^{r-2}(G,M̌) and H^r(G, I⊗M̌) ≅ ⊕_p Ĥ^{r-2}(G_p,M̌). This yields the exact sequence
⊕_p Ĥ^{-1}(G_p,M̌) -> Ĥ^{-1}(G,M̌) -> H²(G, H(K)) -> ⊕_p Ĥ^0(G_p,M̌) -> Ĥ^0(G,M̌).
In this sequence:
- Ĥ^{-1} = Ker(N_G)/I_G M̌; he identifies it with the coinvariants M̌_G in the 'connected' case.
- Ĥ^0(G_p,M̌) = M̌^{G_p}/N_{G_p}M̌.

4. He identifies the local terms with H²(Q_p,H°) ≅ H²(Q_p,H/μ2).

5. At the real place, complex conjugation acts on weight-0 Weil numbers by inversion. So the archimedean terms embed into, or are contained in, M̌/2M̌.

6. He writes the sequence H/μ2 -> G/μ2 -> G' -> 0 with G' ≅ G_m × Ẑ (weight and Frobenius degree).

7. Lower half of the page:
- Γ°/(roots of unity) ≅ M embeds into the free module ⊕ Z over the primes p_1, p̄_1, ..., p_ν, p̄_ν above p. The embedding is given by p-adic valuations normalised by v(p)=1, and M is stable under the decomposition groups.
- H° is dual to M.
- There is a filtration 0 -> Γ°/μ -> Γ/μ·ε*(Z) -> p^{Z/2Z}, with the top quotient detecting the classes of ±p^{1/2}. This corresponds to U° ⊂ U, the U = μ2 × U° of the previous page.
- Final check: if u = ε p^ν (ε a root of unity) is a Weil unit, then weight 0 forces ν=0, so u is a root of unity (Kronecker).

This is essentially the later Langlands–Rapoport/Milne computation of H² of the Weil-number protorus P and its local invariants at p and ∞.
errors: Ĥ^{-1}(G,M̌) = Ker N_G / I_G M̌ is the torsion part of M̌_G, not M̌_G itself. The identification with M̌_G holds only if M̌_G is torsion, presumably what 'H connexe' is meant to guarantee. The note leaves this unjustified.

Passing to the limit over K for a pro-torus with infinitely generated M̌ needs care: Tate–Nakayama applies to finitely generated modules, so a limit argument over finite quotients is required. This is not addressed.
The middle term written 'Ĥ^0(G, M̌⊗Y)' appears to be a struck-through false start. No Tate isomorphism for H²(G, K*⊗M̌) itself exists; it is only computed by the five-term sequence.

ideas.what: Computing H²(Q, T) for a group of multiplicative type via the idèle class sequence and Tate–Nakayama local/global terms
ideas.modern_name: Tate–Nakayama / Poitou–Tate computation of H² of tori (Kottwitz-style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate, Nakayama (1950s); Kottwitz for systematic use in the 1980s

ideas.what: Applying this to the Weil-number protorus (kernel of the motivic Galois group of F_p) to get local invariants at p and ∞, with the archimedean term landing in M̌/2M̌
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology class of the pseudo-motivic Galois gerbe / obstruction to Q-valued fibre functors on motives over F_p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987); Milne, 'Motives over finite fields' (1994); partly Saavedra Rivano (1972)

ideas.what: Weight-0 Weil numbers modulo roots of unity embedded in ⊕Z over the primes above p via normalised p-adic valuations; Kronecker forcing Weil units to be roots of unity
ideas.modern_name: Character group of the Weil-number torus P° described by slopes/valuations at places above p

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck set up the Tate–Nakayama computation of H²(Q, P°) for the Weil-number protorus underlying motives over F_p. He identified the local terms at p (via valuations at the primes above p) and at ∞ (M̌/2M̌), aiming at the class of the motivic gerbe over Q. This anticipates by roughly two decades the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne analysis of the pseudo-motivic Galois gerbe and its local invariants. The calculation is left unfinished on the page.
missed.quote: H²(Q_p, H°) ≃ H²(Q_p, H/μ2) ... pour p=∞, ↪ M̌/2M̌
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the cohomological description of the motivic Galois gerbe of F_p. Shows Grothendieck already viewed the non-neutrality of motives over F_p as an H² class with explicit local components.

deep.surprise_reason: The Weil-number torus as the motivic group of F_p is known to stem from Grothendieck (via Saavedra). An explicit Tate–Nakayama computation of H² with local terms at p and ∞, prefiguring Langlands–Rapoport's gerbe, is a notable but sketchy and unfinished unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: The first line most likely reads H²(Q, H), with H the group dual to the weight-0 Weil numbers, consistent with the later H°, H/μ2. It is probably not T.
'Ĥ^0(G, M̌⊗Y)' is likely a struck/aborted term, not a genuine group.
'identifié avec M̌_G si H connexe' sits in a margin note attached to Ker(M̌ -> M̌^G).
'pour p=∞, c→ M̌/2M̌ dans les cas connexes' (the archimedean term injects into M̌/2M̌).
